topic: Akainu chased Luffy through Ace because Ace's lineage, not power, was the real target
title: Akainu Aimed Past Ace At Luffy
description: Akainu insulted Whitebeard to stop Ace in his tracks, then did something most fans miss: he aimed his final attack straight at Luffy, not down at Ace. Here's why that single choice reveals the entire reason for Marineford.
comment: Was Akainu trying to stop Ace from reaching Whitebeard, or was he aiming at Luffy the whole time?

lines.text: Akainu insulted the Emperor. Ace couldn't stand it and turned around to fight.
But watch what actually happens when Ace charges him in chapter 573.

shot.fallback: fire pirate attacking a magma admiral

lines.text: Akainu catches the attack and aims his magma right past Ace's body.
His real target was never in front of him. It was directly behind him.

shot.fallback: admiral's aim passing through one body

lines.text: He says both the Roger lineage and the Dragon lineage deserve the same sentence, and he means it as law.
Ace throws himself in front to shield Luffy, and that single choice decides everything that happens next.
The whole war was built around one decision: erase a lineage, not stop an Emperor.
And Akainu aimed past Ace to make sure...

self_check.hook: line 1 immediately sets the action (Akainu insulting Whitebeard), line 2 names the chapter to verify, lines 3-4 state the claim (Akainu aimed at Luffy, not Ace)
